newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended steady in hushed cautious trade as the United States' Federal Open Market Committee met to decide on a possible interest hike.
"The market has been quiet ahead of the U.S. meeting on the interest rates situation...it ended flat," one dealer said.
Dealers said the gold price, trading above $351 per ounce, rekindled limited interest in golds in afternoon trade, but the golds index ended flat.
Some institutional buying of select stocks was seen at lower levels. Volumes were moderate at 613 million rand worth.
Dealers said the market would look to Wall Street for direction on Thursday, although a quarter percentage rise in interest rates was already discounted.
They said the market would possibly rise on Wednesday after an announcement in line with expectations, but gains were seen capped by lethargy ahead of the Easter long-weekend.
"The market will be relieved that it is over...it will remain positive, but quiet until the Easter holidays," Johan Marais, director at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
The overall index ended up 0.6 points to 7,079.5 points, the industrial index gained 11.9 points to 8,340.3 points and the gold index made 0.3 points to 1,326.0 points.
Among blue chip shares Anglo added 125 cents to 271.50 rand, Nedcor was up 50 cents to 84.50 rand, Sasol slipped 50 cents to 49.75 rand and Remgro ended up 80 cents to 45.70 rand.
On the gold index Dries was down 50 cents to 41.05 rand, Eastvaal added 28 cents to 610 rand, Western Deep lost 300 cents to 132 rand and JCI dropped 250 cents to 43 rand.

South African equity index futures bounced up slightly awaiting the decision of the FOMC. Gold contracts were also marginally up on the bullion price, but the market failed to react to Wall Street's overnight 100 point surge.
The June all-share contract was at 6,530/40 from 6,525, the industrial contract was at 8,155/62 from 8,147 and the gold contract was at 920/40 from 925.
